who: Historian of twentieth-century Canada at the University of Toronto; PhD, York University.

evidence.says: The indexed faculty profile identifies Steve Penfold as a Toronto history professor specializing in twentieth-century Canada, with a PhD from York University.
The authority for Steven Penfold cites The Workers’ Festival (2005), whose title page names Steve Penfold and identifies him as an assistant professor of history at the University of Toronto.

notes: LC explicitly bridges Steven and Steve at the same department; the faculty profile also matches the AHA doctorate institution. The PhD year was not independently confirmed.

who: Labor and political historian at the University of Arkansas; PhD, Ohio State University, 1999.

evidence.says: The public ORCID record names Michael Pierce and contains a University of Arkansas asserted employment entry: associate professor, Department of History, beginning in 2011.
The 2006–2007 departmental newsletter reports that Pierce earned his Ohio State PhD in 1999, writing on industrial labor and American Populism.
The department lists Arley Ward’s 2021 dissertation, [Dis]Assembling Race: The FEPC in Oklahoma, 1941–1946, with Michael Pierce as advisor.

notes: The candidate ORCID, doctorate institution and year, and an exact AHA student/advisor pairing agree.

who: Historian of African American history and the U.S. South at the University of Georgia; PhD, University of Virginia.

evidence.says: Robert A. Pratt joined Georgia’s history faculty in 1987 and holds a PhD from Virginia. His graduate students include Marvin Chiles, Christopher Huff and Robert Luckett, matching all three AHA students.
The Robert A. Pratt authority cites The Color of Their Skin and Georgia’s faculty page, identifying him as a professor in its History Department.

notes: The authority directly identifies the Georgia professor, whose own department names all three students. The PhD institution matches; its year was not independently confirmed.

who: Historian of twentieth-century U.S. public policy and urban history at the University at Buffalo; PhD, Columbia, 1989.

evidence.says: Buffalo’s History Department identifies Gail Radford as a professor, lists her fields in twentieth-century U.S. history and public policy, and gives her doctorate as Columbia, 1989.
The Gail Radford authority cites Modern Housing for America (1996), identifying its author as an assistant professor of history at SUNY Buffalo.

notes: The candidate authority and faculty profile identify the same historian at Buffalo; the doctorate institution and year exactly match AHA.

who: Historian of U.S. women, urban life and consumer culture at Clark University; PhD in history, New York University, 2000.

evidence.says: Clark’s profile gives Amy Richter’s history PhD as New York University, 2000, and lists Home on the Rails (2005) among her books.
Clark identifies Melinda Marchand as a 2020 PhD graduate and explicitly names Amy Richter as her dissertation advisor.
The authority for Amy G. Richter cites Home on the Rails (2005), matching the book on Clark’s faculty profile.

notes: The book links Amy G. Richter to Clark’s Amy Richter; the doctorate and Marchand supervision independently match AHA.

who: Historian of Spanish and European economic history at UC San Diego; PhD, University of Wisconsin, 1966.

evidence.says: The David R. Ringrose authority cites a UC San Diego notice: Wisconsin PhD in 1966, joined its History Department in 1974, and taught Spanish and world history there for 34 years.
UC San Diego’s history faculty list identifies David R. Ringrose with a Wisconsin PhD, 1966, specializing in early modern Europe and Spanish economic history.
Kevin Ingram’s UC San Diego history dissertation, Secret Lives, Public Lies, identifies Professor David Ringrose as committee chair; its title page and abstract give 2006.

notes: The authority, doctorate and direct supervision record agree. Ingram’s dissertation gives 2006 rather than AHA’s 2007; this does not affect the supervisor identity.

who: Historian of Mexican American and urban history, formerly at the University of Texas at Austin; PhD in history, UCLA, 1975.

evidence.says: Berkeley’s oral-history catalogue describes Ricardo Romo as a historian with a UCLA history PhD in 1975, later holding faculty positions at UC San Diego and UT Austin; it lists East Los Angeles: History of a Barrio among his works.
UT Austin identifies Ricardo Romo as supervisor of Ramona Houston’s 2000 dissertation on the desegregation of Texas and as co-supervisor of Kenneth Mason’s Paternal Continuity.
The Ricardo Romo authority identifies him as author of East Los Angeles (1983), matching the historian described by Berkeley.

notes: The candidate’s work and exact UCLA doctorate match; UT Austin directly confirms two of the listed supervision relationships.

who: Historian of Hungary and twentieth-century international relations at the University of Cincinnati; PhD in history, Indiana University, 1971.

evidence.says: His own site identifies him as Thomas L. Sakmyster, gives his Indiana history PhD in 1971 and Cincinnati appointments from 1971 to 2005, and lists Hungary’s Admiral on Horseback (1994).
The OhioLINK record for Natasha Margulis’s 2004 Cincinnati history PhD, Njegoš’s Montenegro, the Great Powers, and Modernization in the Balkans, names Thomas Sakmyster as advisor.
The authority for Thomas L. Sakmyster cites Hungary’s Admiral on Horseback (1994), whose title page uses Thomas Sakmyster.

notes: The authority bridges the name variants through the same book; the doctorate, faculty period and exact Margulis supervision match AHA.
